page: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a GPU-accelerated virtual server within the Cloud GPU family. It features an Intel x86_64 processor with 8 shared vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 40.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB per core. For storage, it includes a 740 GB local NVMe SSD. The primary accelerator is a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with a 0.3333 allocation, providing 16 GB of dedicated VRAM.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard CPU and memory operations, with a PassMark CPU score of 14090.9 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 14175.12. However, the fractional NVIDIA A40 GPU delivers top-tier performance for specific workloads. Large language model inference speeds reach 9944.32 tokens per second for prompt processing and 464.42 tokens per second for text generation using a small 135M model. For a medium 7B model, the server achieves 3147.67 tokens per second for prompt processing and 107.73 tokens per second for text generation. Memory bandwidth is measured at 784.94 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 88.57 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads.

This server offers a qualitative cost-efficiency advantage for workloads requiring GPU acceleration without the overhead of a full dedicated GPU, utilizing a partitioned A40 instance. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and a moderate 2.0 GHz clock speed, which limits raw single-core CPU performance, as reflected in the average stress-ng single-core score of 1786.68. The hardware configuration is suited for medium-scale LLM inference, machine learning model deployment, database operations, and applications requiring local NVMe storage alongside GPU-accelerated compute.
